assumptions.condition: \(Z\perp\!\!\perp(D_s(0),D_s(1),(Y_s(z,d))_{z,d\in\{0,1\}})\mid X=x\) and \(P_s(Z=1\mid X=x)=e_s(x)\) for every \(s\) and \(x\in\mathcal H_s\).

standard.name: Conditional ITT-effect transportability across a collection

novel.justification: This cross-source compliance-ITT transport condition is scientifically plausible when the encouragement, access channel, eligibility rule, and treatment definition are protocol-invariant across sites after conditioning on the finite baseline cells. It lets different trials supply the target first stage on the cells they cover. Rudolph and van der Laan instead observe receipt in the target site and identify their CACE denominator from the target-site instrument-to-receipt regression; the present condition replaces that target-site first-stage data with a collection-wide transport restriction.

assumptions.condition: \(0<p_0\le1\) and \(p_s(x)\ge p_0\) for every \(s\) and \(x\in\mathcal H_s\).

novel.justification: This is the weakest score-level lower-variance form used by the uniform inversion: it requires only the sum of the two propensity-scaled arm variances to stay nondegenerate, not a positive lower bound in each arm. It is satisfied when every supported cell has outcome measurement or biological noise in at least one randomized arm uniformly over the bounded null index. Bounded outcomes, binary receipt, and propensity overlap provide the upper variance bound, so no substantive causal restriction is added beyond preventing degenerate studentization.

This paper-specific collection-strength class groups laws by target compliance relative to the exact support-constrained observed-data variance. It is an interpretable design index: two trial portfolios with the same compliance can lie in different classes because precision is attached to different target cells. The class includes weak, intermediate, and strong compliance sequences by varying \(u\); it does not impose a stronger causal model.

definitions.name: source support hyperedges
definitions.construction: \(p_s(x)=P_s(X=x)\) and \(\mathcal H_s=\{x\in\mathcal X:p_s(x)>0\}\) for \(s=1,\ldots,K\).

definitions.name: target-cell ITT contrasts
definitions.construction: \(\delta_D(x)=E_{P_T}[D_T(1)-D_T(0)\mid X=x]\) and \(\delta_Y(x)=E_{P_T}[Y_T(1,D_T(1))-Y_T(0,D_T(0))\mid X=x]\).

definitions.name: target ITT numerator and denominator
definitions.construction: \(\mu_Y=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_T(x)\delta_Y(x)\) and \(\mu_D=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_T(x)\delta_D(x)\).

definitions.name: transported complier effect
definitions.construction: \(\theta_T=\mu_Y/\mu_D\) on \(\{P:\mu_D>0\}\).

definitions.name: null residual and cell price
definitions.construction: \(r_\theta=Y-\theta D\) and \(q_{sx}(\theta)=\operatorname{Var}_{P_s}(r_\theta\mid X=x,Z=1)/e_s(x)+\operatorname{Var}_{P_s}(r_\theta\mid X=x,Z=0)/\{1-e_s(x)\}\).

definitions.name: collection allocation polytope
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{coll}}(p_T,\mathcal H)=\{a\in\mathbb R_+^{K\times|\mathcal X|}:a_{sx}=0\text{ if }x\notin\mathcal H_s,\ \sum_{s=1}^K a_{sx}=p_T(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal X\}\).

definitions.name: allocated and optimized collection variance
definitions.construction: \(W_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta,a)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\sum_{s=1}^K a_{sx}^2q_{sx}(\theta)/\{n_sp_s(x)\}\) and \(V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta)=\min_{a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{coll}}(p_T,\mathcal H)}W_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta,a)\).

definitions.name: collection concentration index
definitions.construction: \(T_{\mathrm{coll}}(P)=\mu_D^2/V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta_T)\).

definitions.name: exact pooled observed-data experiment
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{coll}}(P)=\bigotimes_{s=1}^K P_s^{\otimes n_s}\) on the labeled blocks \(O_{si}=(X_{si},Z_{si},D_{si},Y_{si})\), retaining each known source propensity \(e_s(x)\), each support \(\mathcal H_s\), and the fixed target composition \(p_T\).

definitions.name: base transported encouragement class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_N=\{P=(P_1,\ldots,P_K,P_T):P\text{ satisfies the listed member properties for the triangular array indexed by }N\}\).

definitions.name: collection-strength class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_N(u)=\{P\in\mathcal M_N:T_{\mathrm{coll}}(P)\ge u\}\).

definitions.name: uniformly honest interval class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak C_{N,\alpha}=\{C_N:\liminf_{N\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_N:\mu_D(P)>0}P\{\theta_T(P)\in C_N\}\ge1-\alpha,\ C_N\text{ is a data-measurable closed interval in }[-1,1]\}\).

definitions.name: all-procedure minimax expected length
definitions.construction: \(R_{N,\alpha}(u)=\inf_{C_N\in\mathfrak C_{N,\alpha}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_N(u)}E_P[\ell(C_N)]\), where \(\ell(C)=\sup C-\inf C\) for nonempty \(C\) and \(\ell(\varnothing)=0\).

definitions.name: fully empirical collection profiler
definitions.construction: For each \(\theta\in[-1,1]\), compute \(\widehat p_s(x)\), randomized-arm means of \(Y-\theta D\), and arm sample variances. Let \(\widehat q_{sx}(\theta)\) be the plug-in cell price, replace it by \(8/e_0\) when either arm count is below two, and floor every other computed value at \(N^{-1/2}\). Define \(\widehat a(\theta)\) as a measurable minimizer of \(\sum_{s,x}a_{sx}^2\widehat q_{sx}(\theta)/\{n_s\max(\widehat p_s(x),N^{-1})\}\) over \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{coll}}(p_T,\mathcal H)\).

definitions.name: profiled null score and variance
definitions.construction: \(\widehat m_N(\theta)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\sum_{s=1}^K\widehat a_{sx}(\theta)\{\overline r_{sx1}(\theta)-\overline r_{sx0}(\theta)\}\) and \(\widehat V_N(\theta)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\sum_{s=1}^K\widehat a_{sx}(\theta)^2\widehat q_{sx}(\theta)/\{n_s\max(\widehat p_s(x),N^{-1})\}\).

definitions.name: profiled Anderson--Rubin inversion
definitions.construction: \(\mathrm{AR}_N(\theta)=\widehat m_N(\theta)^2/\widehat V_N(\theta)\) and \(C_N^{\mathrm{AR}}=\operatorname{hull}\{\theta\in[-1,1]:\mathrm{AR}_N(\theta)\le\chi^2_{1,1-\alpha}\}\), with \(\operatorname{hull}(\varnothing)=\varnothing\).

definitions.name: two-cell split-support Rademacher family
definitions.construction: For each \(n\), set \(K=2\), \(\mathcal X=\{x_1,x_2\}\), \(n_1=n_2=n\), \(p_T(x_1)=p_T(x_2)=1/2\), \(\mathcal H_1=\{x_1\}\), \(\mathcal H_2=\{x_2\}\), \(p_j(x_j)=1\), and \(e_j(x_j)=1/2\). In source \(j\), draw independent \(C\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\mu_n)\) and Rademacher \(\varepsilon\); set \(D_j(0)=0\), \(D_j(1)=C\), and \(Y_j(z,d)=1/2+\varepsilon/(2\sqrt2)\) for all \(z,d\). Give the target the equally weighted mixture of the cell laws and denote the law by \(P_n^{\mathrm{split}}\).

definitions.name: paired-versus-mixed precision collections
definitions.construction: For each \(n\), set \(K=4\), \(n_s=n\), \(\mathcal X=\{x_1,x_2\}\), \(p_T(x_1)=p_T(x_2)=1/2\), \(p_s(x)=1\) on the unique supported cell, and \(e_s(x)=1/2\). In every source draw \(C_s\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\mu_n)\) and an independent Rademacher \(\varepsilon_s\); set \(D_s(0)=0\), \(D_s(1)=C_s\), and \(Y_s(z,d)=1/2+\varepsilon_s\sqrt{q_s}/2\). Set \(D_T(0)=0\), draw \(D_T(1)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\mu_n)\) independently within each target cell, and set \(Y_T(z,d)=1/2\). In \(P_n^A\), sources \(1,2\) cover \(x_1\) with \(q_s=q_L\), while sources \(3,4\) cover \(x_2\) with \(q_s=q_H\). In \(P_n^B\), sources \(1,3\) cover \(x_1\) and sources \(2,4\) cover \(x_2\), with \(q_1=q_2=q_L\) and \(q_3=q_4=q_H\).

definitions.name: least-favorable collection experiment handle
definitions.construction: Begin at \(P_n^{\mathrm{split}}\). For a local displacement \(h\), tilt the Rademacher probability of the complier receipt-zero outcome by an amount proportional to \(h\), and counter-tilt the never-taker receipt-zero probability by \(\mu_nh/(1-\mu_n)\), preserving the control-arm mixture. For a general support face, apply these compensated tilts cellwise with signed amplitudes selected from the dual of \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{coll}}(p_T,\mathcal H)\); this is the route to the quadratic observed-law experiment \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{coll}}(P)\).

definitions.name: exact-constant method handle
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{sharp}}\) denotes the route that proves Le Cam convergence of the support-preserving continuum to \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{coll}}(P)\) and then applies ordered-modulus acceptance-region optimization on \([-1,1]\).

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_N\) with \(\mu_D>0\), \[E_{P_T}[Y_T(1,D_T(1))-Y_T(0,D_T(0))\mid D_T(1)>D_T(0)]=\theta_T=\frac{\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_T(x)\delta_Y(x)}{\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_T(x)\delta_D(x)},\] and every cell contrast is identified from each source covering that cell.
statements.justification: This links the statistical ratio to the target causal effect among compliers.
statements.gap: Dahabreh et al., Theorem 1, identify target potential-outcome means under their baseline conditions; Theorems 2 and 3 give weaker collection-positivity routes, with Theorem 3 using the cell-specific trial subsets of Section 3.4.2. They do not identify or analyze a weakly identified noncompliance ratio. Rudolph and van der Laan use receipt observed in the target site for their CACE first stage, whereas the novel compliance-ITT transport condition here assembles that first stage from covering source trials.
statements.consumer: The five-site Moving to Opportunity analysis can use different trials to supply different target cells.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_N\) and \(\theta\in[-1,1]\), the semiparametric variance bound for \(\mu_Y-\theta\mu_D\) in the exact labeled experiment \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{coll}}(P)\), with its source-specific propensities \(e_s(x)\), is exactly \(V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta)\). Consequently, at \(\theta=\theta_T\) the local information for the ratio coordinate is \(\mu_D^2/V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta_T)=T_{\mathrm{coll}}(P)\). If \(\{x:p_T(x)>0\}\not\subseteq\mathcal H_s\) for every \(s\), no score measurable with respect to any single source block can represent the pathwise derivative of \(\mu_Y-\theta\mu_D\) while retaining the observed supports: every feasible representer must have nonzero components in at least two source blocks. Thus a collection-only-support law is outside every support-retaining single-source fixed-geometry experiment, rather than an algebraic reparameterization of one.
statements.justification: This identifies the collection program with the exact pooled observed-data information and gives a formal non-subsumption criterion for collection-only support.
statements.gap: Dahabreh et al. identify transported means under union support, and Su et al. optimize regular multi-source weights, but neither derives the source-specific-propensity information bound for a null residual or proves failure of every support-retaining single-source representation.
statements.consumer: A trial repository can decide whether its evidence geometry is genuinely collection-only before applying a single-source weak-IV analysis.

statements.statement: For \(P\in\mathcal M_N\), the support-preserving continuum \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{coll}}(P)\) can be chosen so that its local log-likelihood quadratic for a ratio displacement \(h\) is comparable, with constants depending only on the class constants, to \(h^2T_{\mathrm{coll}}(P)\). Hence the squared inverse local testing radius at \(\theta_T\) is comparable to \(T_{\mathrm{coll}}(P)\), and the necessity geometry is the same support-constrained quadratic form \(V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta_T)\) as the exact pooled efficiency bound.
statements.justification: This makes the collection program both an attainable score variance and an all-procedure information modulus.
statements.gap: Su et al. optimize regular source weights, while Cai and Low study an abstract modulus; neither derives this causal support-constrained observed-law modulus.
statements.consumer: Trial collections can be ranked even when no single trial covers the target.

statements.statement: The empirical profiled inversion satisfies \[\liminf_{N\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_N:\mu_D(P)>0}P\{\theta_T(P)\in C_N^{\mathrm{AR}}\}\ge1-\alpha.\] This holds uniformly across changes and ties in the minimizing allocation without consistent estimation of a selected oracle optimizer.
statements.justification: The result supplies implementable coverage through weak compliance and collection-only overlap.
statements.gap: Ma's Theorem 3.2 controls one orthogonal LATE score, not a null-indexed estimated collection value and its allocation-face transitions.
statements.consumer: Multi-site analysts can avoid compliance pretests and oracle source weights.

statements.statement: For a finite \(C_\alpha>0\) depending only on \(\alpha\) and the fixed class constants, \[\limsup_{N\to\infty}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_N(u)}\frac{E_P[\ell(C_N^{\mathrm{AR}})]}{\min\{1,u^{-1/2}\}}\le C_\alpha\] uniformly over admissible \(u=u_N>0\) with nonempty \(\mathcal M_N(u)\).
statements.justification: The confidence interval automatically shortens at the collection-information rate.
statements.gap: Weak-IV inversion results do not establish bounded-ratio expected-length rates under a trial-support hypergraph.
statements.consumer: Evidence-synthesis teams can value a trial that covers only selected target cells.

statements.statement: If \(0<p_0\le1\), \(0<\mu_n\le1\), \(e_0\le1/2\), \(\rho_0\le1/2\), and \(v_0\le1/2\), then \(P_n^{\mathrm{split}}\in\mathcal M_{2n}\), \(\theta_T=0\), and \(\mu_D=\mu_n\). The allocation is \(a_{1x_1}=a_{2x_2}=1/2\), with all other coordinates zero. Since \(\operatorname{Var}(Y\mid X=x_j,Z=z)=1/8\), \(q_{jx_j}(0)=1/2\), and \[V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P_n^{\mathrm{split}},0)=2\frac{(1/2)^2(1/2)}{n}=\frac1{4n},\qquad T_{\mathrm{coll}}(P_n^{\mathrm{split}})=4n\mu_n^2.\] A CACE displacement \(h\) along the compensated Rademacher route has bounded pairwise observed-law divergence whenever \(n\mu_n^2h^2\) is bounded.
statements.justification: The exact membership audit and arithmetic calibrate the smallest collection-only least-favorable family.
statements.gap: This is a calibration lemma, not a root novelty claim; it verifies the weak-compliance scale under genuinely legal class constants, including \(0<p_0\le1\).
statements.consumer: A two-site planner obtains an explicit benchmark when each site covers only one target cell.

statements.statement: Let \(0<p_0\le1\), \(0<v_0\le q_L<q_H\le1\), \(e_0\le1/2\), \(\rho_0\le1/4\), and \(0<\mu_n\le1\). Then \(P_n^A,P_n^B\in\mathcal M_{4n}\). They have the same \(N=4n\), \(K=4\), target composition, aggregate compliance \(\mu_D=\mu_n\), source sample sizes, source cell masses, propensities, and labeled multiset of per-source prices \(\{q_L,q_L,q_H,q_H\}\), and neither collection contains a source covering both target cells. Nevertheless, \[V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P_n^A,0)=\frac{q_L+q_H}{8n}>\frac{q_Lq_H}{2n(q_L+q_H)}=V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P_n^B,0),\qquad V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P_n^A,0)-V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P_n^B,0)=\frac{(q_H-q_L)^2}{8n(q_L+q_H)}.\] Therefore their exact pooled observed-data information bounds \(1/V_{\mathrm{coll}}\), their collection strengths, and their strong-branch honest-length benchmarks are strictly different. No scalar single-source or Kish-style reduction based on pooled size, aggregate compliance, target composition, and marginal per-source precision summaries can represent both collections while retaining observed support; the joint incidence of precision and cell support is necessary.
statements.justification: This strict-separation corollary of the pooled-information equivalence is non-definitional: the source-by-cell precision incidence, rather than a pooled effective sample size, controls inference.
statements.gap: Published multi-source efficiency formulas do not exhibit two collection-only encouragement designs matched on scalar summaries but separated by the support-constrained residual program.
statements.consumer: Trial portfolio design must match precise sources to target cells rather than report only total enrollment or a Kish effective size.

statements.statement: For some \(c_\alpha>0\) depending only on \(\alpha\) and the fixed class constants, every uniformly honest interval obeys \[\liminf_{N\to\infty}\inf_{C_N\in\mathfrak C_{N,\alpha}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_N(u)}\frac{E_P[\ell(C_N)]}{\min\{1,u^{-1/2}\}}\ge c_\alpha\] for every admissible \(u=u_N>0\) with nonempty \(\mathcal M_N(u)\). The split-support continuum has \(V_{\mathrm{coll}}=1/(4n)\), \(T_{\mathrm{coll}}=4n\mu_n^2\), and bounded divergence at CACE displacement \(h\asymp\min\{1,T_{\mathrm{coll}}^{-1/2}\}\). Cellwise dual compensated tilts extend the construction to every allocation face and yield Kullback--Leibler geometry dual to \(V_{\mathrm{coll}}\).
statements.justification: The result covers all confidence procedures and makes the collection quadratic program necessary.
statements.gap: Cai and Low give general testing machinery, but no published lower family preserves encouragement randomization, exclusion, monotonicity, transport, and union support while inducing this program.
statements.consumer: The theorem rules out pooled and single-source procedures that claim uniform gains over collection profiling.

statements.statement: For fixed \(0<\alpha<1/2\), \[R_{N,\alpha}(u)\asymp_\alpha\min\{1,u^{-1/2}\}\] uniformly over admissible \(u=u_N>0\) for which \(\mathcal M_N(u)\) is nonempty.
statements.justification: One collection information index governs honest precision from weak compliance through the regular regime.
statements.gap: No published result gives an all-procedure confidence-length frontier for a bounded transported CACE under union-of-trials support.
statements.consumer: The allocation value becomes a planning and reporting diagnostic for multi-trial transported CACE.

statements.statement: If \(K=1\) and \(p_T(x)>0\Rightarrow p_1(x)>0\), then \(a_{1x}=p_T(x)\) uniquely and \[V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\frac{p_T(x)^2q_{1x}(\theta)}{n_1p_1(x)}.\] Thus the collection objects reduce algebraically to their one-source residual-variance forms.
statements.justification: This is the required \(K=1\) sanity check.
statements.gap: No novelty or procedural equivalence is claimed for this algebraic corollary.
statements.consumer: Single-trial analyses recover the familiar inverse-cell-mass formula.

statements.statement: Along every sequence in \(\mathcal M_N\) with \(\inf_N\mu_D>0\), the canonical gradient for \(\theta_T\) is the minimum-variance allocated influence score for \(Y-\theta_TD\), divided by \(\mu_D\), and its source-sample variance is \(V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta_T)/\mu_D^2\). The profiled Anderson--Rubin interval is first-order equivalent to the efficient Wald interval generated by \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}\).
statements.justification: The identification-robust procedure remains efficient under strong compliance.
statements.gap: Rudolph and van der Laan derive a single-source ratio gradient, while Su et al. derive multi-source weights for a nonratio effect; neither gives the joint residual allocation.
statements.consumer: Regular multi-site analyses sacrifice no first-order precision by using robust inversion.

statements.statement: Does \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{coll}}(P)\) determine \(\kappa_\alpha\) such that \(R_{N,\alpha}(u)/\min\{1,u^{-1/2}\}\to\kappa_\alpha\) uniformly on compact nondegenerate faces of \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{coll}}(p_T,\mathcal H)\), and can an inversion derived through \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{sharp}}\) attain it while retaining honesty at face transitions?
statements.justification: The rate theorem does not determine the exact confidence-length constant or optimal test shape.
statements.gap: Mikusheva studies invariant weak-IV geometry and Cai and Low sharp Gaussian moduli, but neither covers causal allocation-face transitions.
statements.consumer: An exact constant would compare collections with similar rate indices but different finite-strength geometry.

sampling_model.design: \(K\) independent randomized encouragement trials, source block \(s\) containing \(n_s\) i.i.d. observations, with externally fixed target composition.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary encouragement has known \(e_s(x)\); receipt and outcome satisfy consistency, exclusion, and monotonicity.
sampling_model.overlap: \(0<p_0\le1\), \(p_s(x)\ge p_0\) on \(\mathcal H_s\), randomized-arm overlap holds, and \(\operatorname{supp}(p_T)\subseteq\bigcup_s\mathcal H_s\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Finite-cell frequencies, arm means, and residual variances are empirical. A deterministic floor and bounded fallback make profiling total; no unique oracle optimizer is required.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 identifies target potential-outcome means under conditions A1--A5; Theorem 2 uses weaker collection-level positivity; Theorem 3 uses cell-specific trial subsets and union support; and Theorem 4 identifies an average treatment effect under exchangeability in effect measure.
Equation (4) identifies a single-source transported CACE whose denominator is the instrument-to-receipt contrast in the target site, and Result 3 gives its efficient influence curve.
Theorem 3.2 establishes uniformly correct asymptotic size for an orthogonalized Anderson--Rubin LATE test.
Lemma 2 derives the efficient influence function and optimal source weights for a regular multi-source target average treatment effect.
The paper constructs weak-IV-robust inverted confidence sets and analyzes expected arc length in an invariant circular model.
Theorems 1--3 use ordered moduli to bound and construct honest confidence intervals for linear functionals over nested classes.
The paper identifies and regularly estimates a target-population CACE from a single study.

tldr: A transported complier effect is identified when target cells are covered only by the union of randomized encouragement trials, but honest precision depends on where residual precision lies in the support hypergraph. The collection index \(T_{\mathrm{coll}}=\mu_D^2/V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta_T)\) uses the value of a constrained source-cell variance program, and \(1/V_{\mathrm{coll}}\) is the exact information in the labeled pooled observed-data experiment. A fully empirical profiled Anderson--Rubin inversion is uniformly honest and attains expected length of order \(\min\{1,T_{\mathrm{coll}}^{-1/2}\}\); a support-preserving continuum supplies the all-procedure lower bound. Two matched four-source collections have different values solely because precision is paired with support differently, proving that collection-only geometry is not a support-retaining single-source or Kish-style scalar reduction.

project_justification.gap: Dahabreh et al., Theorems 1--4, identify transported potential-outcome means or average effects under several exchangeability and positivity regimes; Section 3.4.2 and Theorem 3 provide the precise cell-specific trial-subset and union-support logic. Weak-IV theory establishes honest inversion for single moment systems. Neither literature characterizes honest confidence length for a transported noncompliance ratio assembled over a source-support hypergraph.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is the observed-law information modulus for a bounded causal ratio under simultaneous weak compliance and union-only trial support.
project_justification.fill: The collection quadratic program is derived as the attainable score variance and the least-favorable testing modulus; an empirical profiled inversion and a continuum lower experiment give matching length rates, while a strict-separation construction proves the program cannot be collapsed to marginal scalar summaries.

related_work: Dahabreh et al. (2023), Theorem 1, identify target potential-outcome means under conditions A1--A5. Their Theorem 2 weakens treatment and participation positivity to the pooled collection conditions A3* and A5*. Section 3.4.2 defines the covariate-specific covering-trial set, and Theorem 3 combines the corresponding exchangeability condition A4\(^{\dagger}\) with union-support condition A5\(^{\dagger}\); this is the precise workflow grounding for collection-only support here. Their Theorem 4 instead identifies an average treatment effect under exchangeability in effect measure A4\(^{\ddagger}\). None of Theorems 1--4 contains a noncompliance ratio, a null-dependent source allocation, or weak-identification length theory. Rudolph and van der Laan (2017), equation (4) and Result 3, identify and efficiently estimate a single-source transported CACE in the five-site Moving to Opportunity application; their denominator uses instrument-to-receipt behavior observed in the target site, whereas the novel compliance-ITT transport condition here reconstructs the target first stage from covering source trials. Su et al. (2024), Lemma 2, optimize source weights for a regular nonratio target effect. Ma (2026), Algorithm 2.1 and Theorem 3.2, supplies the orthogonal Anderson--Rubin principle for LATE; the all-null score-price nondegeneracy here is a novel paper condition and is not attributed to Ma. Andrews and Mikusheva (2016) treat a null-indexed functional nuisance. Mikusheva (2010) is conceptual precedent for weak-IV strength indexing and robust confidence-set geometry, but does not define \(T_{\mathrm{coll}}\) or the collection strength floor. Cai and Low (2004) give ordered-modulus expected-length tools. These results inform the construction; no strict extension of their model-specific theorems is claimed.
technical_internal_limitation: The target composition \(p_T\) is externally fixed. A random target sample for a superpopulation estimand contributes an additional target-composition influence term to \(V_{\mathrm{coll}}\). The finite-cell model also excludes high-dimensional nuisance learning.
honest_scope: Identification, exact pooled-information equivalence, non-subsumption by support-retaining single-source geometry, uniform coverage, matching expected-length rate, strict collection separation, regular efficiency, and membership of the explicit least-favorable families are to be proved. The \(K=1\) result is only an algebraic sanity check. The exact minimax constant remains open. The compliance-ITT transport restriction and the collection-strength class are novel paper conditions; the former replaces target-site receipt data with protocol-invariant first-stage transport across covering sources, and the latter indexes compliance relative to exact collection information. Mikusheva provides only conceptual weak-IV precedent for the latter. The novel variance assumption is the cell-and-score lower bound \(\inf_{\theta}q_{sx}(\theta)\ge v_0\), weaker than armwise lower bounds and used only to keep studentization uniform over the inverted nulls; bounded data and propensity overlap supply its upper counterpart. The class explicitly requires \(0<p_0\le1\), which admits both singleton-support constructions because their supported-cell masses equal one.

novelty_justification: The closest collection result is Dahabreh et al. (2023): Theorem 1 gives baseline mean transport, Theorem 2 weakens pooled positivity, Section 3.4.2 and Theorem 3 formalize cell-specific covering trials and union support, and Theorem 4 gives an effect-measure route for an average effect. None treats a weak noncompliance ratio. The closest causal-ratio result is Rudolph and van der Laan (2017), equation (4) and Result 3, for a regular single-source transported CACE whose first stage is learned from target-site receipt data. The cross-source compliance-ITT transport condition here is therefore explicit and novel. Ma (2026) supplies a one-system robust LATE score, with Mikusheva (2010) providing only conceptual weak-IV precedent for strength indexing; neither supplies \(T_{\mathrm{coll}}\). Su et al. (2024) supplies regular multi-source weights for a nonratio effect. The kernel proves that the exact pooled observed-data information for the null residual is \(1/V_{\mathrm{coll}}\), that collection-only support cannot be represented by a support-retaining single-source fixed geometry, and that \(T_{\mathrm{coll}}\) is the rate index for every honest procedure through a causal continuum lower experiment. The legal split-support family has \(V_{\mathrm{coll}}=1/(4n)\) and \(T_{\mathrm{coll}}=4n\mu_n^2\). More decisively, the paired-versus-mixed four-source constructions match total size, target composition, compliance, supported-cell masses, propensities, and marginal source price summaries but have strictly different \(V_{\mathrm{coll}}\) and \(T_{\mathrm{coll}}\), so the collection geometry cannot be replaced by a pooled or Kish-style scalar.
